finalText:
Two common reasons, and often both at once.

React re-renders a child whenever the parent re-renders, unless the child is wrapped in `React.memo`. Without that wrapper, "same props" doesn't matter — it renders anyway.

Even with `React.memo`, it still re-renders if you're passing a new function, object, or array each time. Things like `onClick={() => ...}` or `style={{...}}` written inline create a brand new value on every render, so React sees it as a different prop even though it looks the same.

The fix is usually `React.memo` on the child, plus `useCallback` for functions and `useMemo` for objects/arrays that you pass down as props.
